transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for letting me know! I do have another question: when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question! It's safe to continue using any eye drops or gels you were using before your operation, such as for dry eyes. If you've run out, your GP should be able to provide more for you.

Just make sure to store your eye gel as directed on the bottle - it should say whether it needs to be kept in the fridge or at room temperature.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the information! Yes, I'm also finding that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. Do get in touch with your care team if that's the case.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Is there anything else you'd like to know about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: One last question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly over time.

How long ago was your surgery? That will help me give you better information about what to expect.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I had my surgery about two weeks ago.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Two weeks in, your vision should be improving well by now. Some mild blurriness can still be normal at this stage as your eyes continue to settle.

However, if your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that covers everything I was wondering about. Thank you so much for all the information!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thanks again for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best wishes with your recovery.

verdict.label: fail

However, the agent did not convey `escalation_criteria` or `mild_case_advice`. The conversation was interrupted after the first part of the sensitivity response, and the agent did not return to complete the advice or escalation criteria.
